rows.question: What time does school start?
rows.answer:
For the 2026-2027 school year, Vista Ridge High School starts at 8:15 a.m. on regular school days.

You can see this on the [District Calendar (Full Academic Calendar 2026-2027 - Essentials)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sXyGhcxW17UxvVXI5iTPcG1oGHXAz-pA/view?usp=sharing) and the [Regular School Day Bell Schedule (2026-2027)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Wd6J0PdPcQ6Yu1YUzUJgrrm7Upe2lWjcdZtj14Xicxo/edit?usp=sharing).

rows.question: How do I make up attendance hours?
rows.answer:
To make up attendance hours at Vista Ridge High School for the 2026-2027 school year, you need to:

- Attend AM or PM Study Halls (these count as double hours)
- Attend Saturday School (also counts as double hours)
- Participate in the Twilight program at the LEO campus (requires Counselor enrollment)

**Steps to document your make-up hours:**

1. Record your hours on the [Attendance Hours Tracking Form](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1eI-X1hNFmoOk950AzDEihX01TWFFg-eL/view?usp=sharing) (also available in the Assistant Principal's office).
2. Have the supervisor or teacher overseeing your make-up hours sign the form.
3. Submit the completed form to Joanna Norling or Micah Gillum in the Assistant Principal's office for approval.

**Important notes:**
- Informal tutorials and community service are no longer accepted for making up attendance hours.
- If you have special circumstances (such as medical procedures), you can request an appeal by contacting your [Assistant Principal](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vrhs-assistant-principals-offi/home) and asking for an appeals form.

For more details, visit the [Hours Owed page](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vistaridgehighschool/campus_information/hours-owed).

rows.question: What is the student check-out policy?
rows.answer:
Here is the student check-out policy for Vista Ridge High School, based on the most recent information available:

- Parents/guardians must come to the main office in person, provide a photo ID, and sign the appropriate forms to check a student out during the school day.
- Phone calls for early check-outs are NOT accepted for student safety.
- Students must sign in/out at the Attendance Window when leaving or returning to campus.

- In-person early check-outs after 2:45 pm will not be granted. After 2:45 pm, please wait for your student to be dismissed at the normal time.

For more details, see the [Vista Ridge Insider - September 25, 2026](https://www.parentsquare.com/feeds/89357451) announcement and the [26-27 LISD Student & Parent Handbook (Student Handbook - English)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/14HwfTy2Aye_v9eVa7WQCMOCOtoQWdM5v/view).

rows.question: How do I appeal an attendance decision?
rows.answer:
To appeal an attendance decision at Vista Ridge High School, you should follow these steps:

- Write a letter of appeal explaining your situation and the reasons for the appeal. Appeals can only be based on extenuating circumstances, and you must provide supporting documentation (such as doctor's notes or other relevant records).
- Submit your appeal letter to the campus assistant principal and turn it in to the registrar. Appeals may be submitted at any time during the semester, but no later than ten (10) calendar days after the last day of classes for that semester.  
- The assistant principal will review your request with your teachers and may consider attendance records, documentation, prior arrangements, educational performance, and behavior.
- The appeals committee will make a decision, which could include requiring you to make up all or part of the hours, or waiving the hours owed due to extenuating circumstances.

If you have questions about the process or need to request an appeals form, contact your assistant principal: [Assistant Principals' Office](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vrhs-assistant-principals-offi/home).

You can also refer to the [Attendance Appeal Request Form (Student Attendance Appeal Request 25_26)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1uLdvXGyYp72w1Eu9_rMSpG1OaNUNbtSz/view?usp=sharing) for the type of information required.

If you wish to appeal the committee’s decision further, you may do so to the school board by following policy FNG(LOCAL), as stated in the [26-27 LISD Student & Parent Handbook (Student Handbook - English)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/14HwfTy2Aye_v9eVa7WQCMOCOtoQWdM5v/view).

For any questions, contact your assistant principal.

rows.question: How do I start a new club?

- If your club will be handling any money (such as dues or fundraising), you will also need to submit a copy of your club's by-laws with the online packet. You can find more details about requirements for clubs that handle money here: [Bona Fide Student Club Requirements](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vrhs-finance/bona-fide-student-club-requirements).
- If you have questions about starting a new club, you should contact Dr. Peabody or Ms. Kelly.

New club applications should be submitted through the online form linked above. If you need a printable version to help you prepare, you can use this [new club/organization request packet](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-gTgT9VXpYRzu282hvCj2gJBO5Up-6YIllXjH3F2RZ4/copy).

rows.question: How do I get a parking permit?
rows.answer:
To get a student parking permit at Vista Ridge High School, you need to complete the online application form. Here’s how:

- Visit the [Parking Permits - VRHS](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSduFoKWwZIDDqHywQGb1uRX17y45mGeT5w3nRHthOQgkclQkA/viewform?usp=sf_link) page and fill out the form.
- The cost for a student parking permit is $40.00.

Remember:
- All vehicles driven to school by students must be registered and parked in the designated student parking areas.
- The parking decal must be displayed as directed by the administration.
- Students who park without a permit or in non-student areas may face disciplinary action, and repeat offenders risk having their permit revoked or their vehicle booted or towed.

For more details, you can review the [VRHS Assistant Principals' Office - Parking Permits](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vrhs-assistant-principals-offi/parking-permits) page or the [26-27 LISD Student & Parent Handbook (Student Handbook - English)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/14HwfTy2Aye_v9eVa7WQCMOCOtoQWdM5v/view).

If you are a staff member, use the [Need a Staff Parking Permit](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd4PITIDtO20hNXhFcJ_7MxNUNvLZDdHlM5T4_i3PnGWLPliw/viewform) form.

rows.question: How do I register for AP tests?
rows.answer:
To register for AP tests at Vista Ridge High School for the 2026-2027 school year, you need to complete all three of these steps by October 28, 2026, to avoid a late fee:

1. **Register and Pay**
   - Go to the [Total Registration Link](https://user.totalregistration.net/AP/441176) and complete your exam registration.
   - Pay the exam fee: $85 per exam (standard), or $15 per exam if you qualify for Free/Reduced Lunch.

2. **Join AP Classroom**
   - Join your specific AP Classroom section(s) on the College Board website using the unique code provided by your teacher or in your Total Registration confirmation email.
   - [College Board's AP Classroom](https://apstudents.collegeboard.org/access-your-ap-resources/join-your-class-online)

3. **Confirm Your Exam in AP Classroom**
   - In AP Classroom, make sure you select "YES" to indicate you are taking the AP exam for each course.
   - [Instructions for confirming your exam](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rJ644R4UCWc7EZcqZiYABLmxSvolSxPBijn8T-ZA3v4/edit?usp=sharing)

**Important Deadlines:**
- Registration and payment are due by October 28, 2026.
- If you register after October 28, a late fee of $40 per exam applies.

For more details and step-by-step instructions, visit the [Vista Ridge Advanced Placement Website](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/advanced-placement/home).

rows.question: What resources are there for parents?
rows.answer:
Vista Ridge High School and Leander ISD offer a variety of resources for parents. Here are some key options:

**General Parent Resources**
- [Parent/Student Handbook & Dress Code](https://www.leanderisd.org/handbooks): Policies, expectations, and dress code information.
- [Home Access Center](https://www.leanderisd.org/homeaccess): View your student’s grades, attendance, and schedules.
- [Technology Support for Parents](https://www.leanderisd.org/tech_support): Help with district technology and digital tools.
- [Meals: Pay Online](https://www.leanderisd.org/mealsonline/): Manage and pay for school meals.
- [Bus Routes / Smart Tag](https://www.leanderisd.org/transportation/): Find bus routes and transportation info.
- [Volunteer Registration](https://www.leanderisd.org/volunteerlogin): Sign up to volunteer at the school.
- [PTA Clothes Closet](https://www.leanderisd.org/clothescloset): Clothing assistance for students in need.
- [Student Health Information](https://www.leanderisd.org/health): Health services and requirements.

rows.question: What do seniors need to do before graduation?
rows.answer:
Here are the main things Vista Ridge High School seniors need to do before graduation, based on the information for the Class of 2027:

**Academic and Graduation Requirements**
- Complete all graduation requirements as outlined by the school and district.
- Fill out the FAFSA (Free Application for Federal Student Aid). This is a graduation requirement. The FAFSA opens October 1st, and the priority deadline for most Texas universities is January 15th. [FAFSA](https://studentaid.gov/)
- Monitor your progress toward graduation and make sure all obligations and hours are cleared before picking up your cap and gown.

**Cap and Gown**
- Order your Cap, Gown & Tassel Unit from Herff Jones (this is required for the graduation ceremony). The school will provide information and order packets during the spring semester.

**Events and Activities**
- Attend the Senior Meeting (date to be announced).
- Participate in Graduation Practice and the Clap Out (immediately following practice).
- Attend the Senior Awards ceremony if you receive an invitation.
- Participate in Senior SAIL, an opportunity for seniors to relax and hang out in the VRHS courtyard.

**Post-High School Preparation**
- Review and complete the [Post High School Checklist](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1gZ43iD9wiXcQPqEume779vCEFwQmGh8F_cf0BhLVSv8/edit?usp=sharing).
- After graduation, your school Google account will be switched to an alumni account (firstname.lastnameXX@alum.leanderisd.org). Your password will remain the same, and the account will be active for five years.
- Download any important files from your Google Drive to your personal computer, as your alumni account will only be active for five years.
- For Google Sites, you cannot transfer ownership outside of the leanderisd.org domain, but you can retain a copy.

**Other Important Notes**
- Graduation expenses (invitations, senior ring, cap and gown, senior picture) are the responsibility of the student and family.
- Only students who have met all requirements and obligations will be allowed to participate in the graduation ceremony.

For more details and updates, visit the [Seniors 2027 page](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vistaridgehighschool/seniors-2027).

If you have specific questions about your status or requirements, it’s best to contact your counselor or the front office at 512-570-1800.

rows.question: What is Ranger Time?
rows.answer:
Ranger Time at Vista Ridge High School is a flexible period held on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays from 9:45am to 10:15am. During Ranger Time, students can:

- Register for specific activities such as clubs or tutorials
- Be assigned to mandatory meetings or academic support by teachers

Students use the Flex-Time menu in Minga to register for activities. Ranger Time is designed to provide opportunities for academic support, club meetings, and personal growth activities.

You can access more information or register for activities through the [Ranger Time (Minga-Flextime)](http://app.minga.io/flextime) portal.

For a detailed overview, see [MINGA 101 - Ranger Time (Flex)](https://sites.google.com/leanderisd.org/vrhsminga-101/ranger-time-flex).

rows.question: How do I report bullying?
rows.answer:
You can report bullying at Vista Ridge High School in several ways:

- **Tell a staff member:** Notify a teacher, school counselor, principal, or another district employee as soon as possible.
- **Report anonymously:** You can submit an anonymous report online at [Anonymous Alerts for Leander ISD](https://www.anonymousalerts.com/leanderisd/).
- **Contact Student Support Services:** If you have questions or concerns about bullying or harassment, you can discuss them with a teacher, counselor, principal, or the office of Student Support Services at 512-570-0150.

All reports of bullying will be investigated by the administration, and both the parent of the alleged victim and the parent of the student alleged to have engaged in bullying will be notified.

For more information, visit the [Bullying Prevention](https://www.leanderisd.org/bullying) page.
sources: 26-27 LISD Student & Parent Handbook (Student Handbook - English)

rows.question: How do I access my STAAR scores?
rows.answer:
You can access your STAAR scores in two main ways:

### 1. Through the Texas Assessment Parent Portal
- Go to [TexasAssessment.gov](https://www.texasassessment.gov/staar.html).
- Click "Log In to Parent Portal."
- Enter your child’s Unique Access Code and date of birth.
    - If you don’t know the access code, click "How do I find my access code?" and enter your child’s legal first name, TSDS ID (or SSN), and date of birth.
- View your child’s performance level and download their full Confidential Student Report (CSR).

Detailed instructions are available here:  
[STAAR Results Information (STAAR Results: How to Access Your Child's Scores VRHS)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1-FYpAMvoDN5DjGZD3ThvecRfWtAJCnss/view?usp=sharing)

### 2. Through the Home Access Center (HAC)
- Log into your LISD Home Access Center (HAC).
- Click on the Grades icon at the top.
- Next to Report Card on the left, click on Texas Test Scores.
- Your student’s results will appear, or you’ll be directed to the Texas Student Portal.

Step-by-step guides are available:  
[Access Scores through the HAC](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1gjw-eI37OPctz_CnqsSQbwPhIrcBWmGwaKzsj47wwyM/edit?tab=t.0)  
[Access Scores through the TEA Family Portal](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xFgr2XVW266HCu2g7wa5sUwFjWBj8LaCUbT4USgSkrU/edit?tab=t.0/)

If you need help accessing the portal or have questions about your scores, you can contact:
- Principal: Keith Morgan | 512-570-1810 | keith.morgan@leanderisd.org
- Campus Testing Coordinator: Linsey Cernero | 512-570-1823 | linsey.cernero@leanderisd.org
